\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بلند} (boland)}{بلند (boland)}]{\fa{بلند} (boland) — long, tall; loud}

\label{lesson:FA-C59-boland}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for fresh, then the Persian for old.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بلند}}
\textbf{\fa{بلند}} — \emph{boland} — \textquotedblleft{}long, tall; loud\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{boland} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed: it continues Middle Persian \emph{buland}, \textquotedblleft{}high\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*b\textsuperscript{h}erǵ\textsuperscript{h}-}, \textquotedblleft{}high\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{boland}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{boland}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for fresh, then the Persian for old, then say \emph{boland} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گرم} (garm)}{گرم (garm)}]{\fa{گرم} (garm) — warm, hot}

\label{lesson:FA-C59-garm}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for long, then the Persian for short.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گرم}}
\textbf{\fa{گرم}} — \emph{garm} — \textquotedblleft{}warm, hot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{garm} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{garm}, \textquotedblleft{}warm\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*g\textsuperscript{w}\textsuperscript{h}er-}, \textquotedblleft{}to heat\textquotedblright{}, the root usually also given for English \emph{warm}.
\end{cousinweb}
